title: AI Builders Digest
subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天的 feed 有一条很清楚的暗线：agent 正在把工作推向两个方向。一边是更具体、更专业的基础设施，Aaron Levie 看到 cyber agent 即将处理海量 token；另一边是人开始重新思考如何和 AI 相处，Guillermo Rauch 讨论指导 AI 的分寸，Ryo Lu 则提醒我们，过早移除困难，也可能一起移除了学习和建立关系的机会。

archive.title: Agent 分寸日报
archive.desc: agent 正在深入安全与工程基础设施，同时也逼着 builder 重新定义判断力、学习和人与人的连接。

footerNote: Source: Follow Builders curated daily digest. Rebuilt from the 2026-10-26 source feeds.

sections.title: Agents Meet the Real World / Agent 进入真实世界
sections.desc: 当 agent 开始处理安全、日志和企业数据，基础设施的规模与风险会一起上升。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie expects 1,000X more tokens to flow through cyber agents soon. The reason is not just more automation: long-running agents, computer use, and models trained deeply on cybersecurity have made it possible for swarms to fan out across tools, logs, enterprise data, and attack surfaces.

His opportunity map is broad: identity, firewalls, networks, code scanning, and data protection. As cyber risk expands beyond what most companies can manually track, agentic defense may be one of the rare areas where offensive and defensive capabilities can improve together.
original: We’ll likely have 1,000X more tokens flowing through cyber agents soon than we do today.
We’ll have agent swarms that can fan out, leverage any security tool, test various perpetuations of attacks, read through logs, process enterprise data for risk level, and more.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 预计，很快会有 1000 倍于今天的 token 流经 cyber agent。变化不只是自动化变多了：long-running agent、computer use，以及针对网络安全深度训练的模型，已经让 agent swarm 能够铺开到各种安全工具、日志、企业数据和攻击面上。
他看到的机会覆盖 identity、firewall、network、code scanning 和 data protection。随着 cyber risk 扩张到大多数公司无法靠人工追踪的规模，agentic defense 可能是少数能让攻防能力一起提升的方向。
original: 很快会有 1000 倍于今天的 token 流经 cyber agent。
agent swarm 可以铺开，调用各种安全工具，测试攻击方式，读取日志，处理企业数据并评估风险。

sections.title: The New Builder Skill / 新的 Builder 能力
sections.desc: 真正稀缺的能力，开始从亲自完成每一步，转向知道什么时候该引导、什么时候该放手。

rewrite: Guillermo Rauch calls the ability to manage guidance the number-one skill he looks for. Sometimes AI knows more and needs room; sometimes it goes off-track, carries the wrong bias, or lacks context and needs tighter direction. The work is not simply prompting harder. It is learning when to intervene.
original: There’ll be times where you over-guide the AI. It knows better than you and is more intelligent than you.
How well you manage this superpower is the #0 skill I look for.

rewrite: Guillermo Rauch 认为，管理引导力度是他最看重的能力。有时 AI 比你知道得更多，需要你给它空间；有时它会跑偏、带着错误偏见，或者缺少上下文，需要你收紧方向。真正的工作不是把 prompt 写得更用力，而是学会什么时候介入。
original: 有时你会过度引导 AI，它比你更懂；有时你又引导得不够，它会跑偏、带着错误偏见或错过上下文。
你如何管理这个超能力，是我最看重的能力。

rewrite: Rauch notices that models are developing an engineering vernacular around words like gate, evidence, culprit, provenance, and contract. His more interesting question is whether productive engineering work eventually needs a minimum viable English: a much smaller shared vocabulary for debugging and understanding existing systems.
original: I oddly love the models' engineering vernacular: gate, evidence, culprit, durable, provenance, contract…
I wonder what the minimum viable English in fact is to be productive.

rewrite: Rauch 注意到，模型正在形成一套工程语汇：gate、evidence、culprit、provenance、contract。更有意思的问题是：高效的工程工作，最终是否只需要一套更小的「minimum viable English」——一组足以调试和理解既有系统的共享词汇。
original: 我莫名喜欢模型的工程语汇：gate、evidence、culprit、durable、provenance、contract……
我在想，真正能让人高效工作的 minimum viable English 到底是什么。

sections.title: What AI Should Not Remove / AI 不该替你拿走的东西
sections.desc: 效率之外，builder 也在重新审视困难、关系和现实世界中的共同创作。

rewrite: Ryo Lu worries that agents make it easy to get results before learning what the difficulty was teaching us. The same convenience can also let us avoid the awkward, slow process of working with other people: disagreeing, repairing, and eventually making something none of us could make alone.

His conclusion is not anti-tool. He wants tools that help us spend more time with the world, find people, share unfinished work, and struggle together—more like a jazz band than the silent static of a server farm.
original: We learn how to get results without necessarily understanding how it works.
I don’t want a life without struggle. I want people to struggle with.

rewrite: Ryo Lu 担心，agent 让我们在还没学会困难原本要教什么之前，就轻松拿到了结果。同样的便利，也可能让我们绕过和别人一起工作的笨拙过程：意见不合、修复关系，最后做出任何一个人都做不出来的东西。
他的结论不是反对工具，而是希望工具帮助我们更多地进入真实世界，找到人，分享未完成的东西，一起经历困难。像一支爵士乐队，而不是服务器农场的无声噪音。
original: 我们学会了如何得到结果，却不一定理解它是怎么工作的。
我不想要没有困难的人生，我想要可以一起经历困难的人。

rewrite: Aditya Agarwal describes a funny side effect of being fully AI-pilled: he treasures offline time with family and friends more. His prescription is simple—dance, take your kids to the park, let the agents cook or not, and celebrate humans.
original: One weird effect of being max AI pilled is that I have started to really treasure IRL time with my family and my friends.
But dear god, celebrate humans.

rewrite: Aditya Agarwal 说，自己彻底 AI-pilled 之后，一个奇怪的副作用是：反而更珍惜和家人朋友在线下相处的时间。放点 techno，和朋友跳舞，带孩子去公园，让 agent 自己忙去吧，最重要的是庆祝人类。
original: 彻底 AI-pilled 的一个奇怪副作用，是我开始更珍惜和家人朋友在线下相处的时间。
但天啊，请庆祝人类。

sections.title: Small Products, Strong Habits / 小产品如何留下来
sections.desc: 一个产品能否留下来，往往不在功能数量，而在它能不能把行为变成习惯。

rewrite: Peter Yang says Once Reading is the only learning app he and his four-year-old have kept using for months. His explanation is refreshingly concrete: a daily parent-child habit, lightweight gamification such as taking a silly photo after each lesson, and a 30-lesson milestone that sends the child books to read independently.
original: It builds a habit where you need to learn with your kid daily
After 30 lessons, Once will send you books for your kid to read by themselves

rewrite: Peter Yang 说，在他和四岁孩子试过的学习 app 里，Once Reading 是唯一坚持用了几个月的。原因很具体：每天和孩子一起学习，课后拍一张搞怪照片这种轻量 gamification，以及完成 30 节课后寄书给孩子独立阅读的里程碑。
original: 它建立了每天必须和孩子一起学习的习惯。
完成 30 节课后，Once 会寄书给孩子，让他们自己阅读。
